mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where this trigger is met in at least 5 out of the last 10 tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a flattening industrial production trend (INDPRO) predicts weakening corporate sales growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND INDPRO monthly change < 0 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 6 out of the last 10 instances where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 4 out of the last 8 periods where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average indicate robust household formation and spending, which historically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.3% AND HOUST > 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 3 out of the last 5 instances where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to profit margin compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < 0 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 3 out of the last 6 periods where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of more than 0.75 percentage points, in the absence of a concurrent GDP contraction, signals a hawkish policy shift that initially shocks markets but ultimately supports the equity risk premium, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.75% AND GDPC1 monthly change > 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 4 out of the last 8 such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A YoY increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) exceeding 5% while consumption growth (GDPC1) remains flat indicates a buildup of household financial assets, which historically precedes positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days as households allocate savings to equities.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change > 5% AND GDPC1 YoY change < 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 3 out of the last 5 periods where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that boosts wage growth and consumer spending, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 4 out of the last 7 periods where this trigger is met.
